label: Covering Maps
notes: This chapter, printed pages 277 to 306, treats covering maps as machines with visible parts: stacks of sheets over evenly covered neighborhoods, lifted paths, monodromy permutations, and a universal cover storing path classes as points. We open with the exponential map R to the circle as the guiding model for every later theorem.

label: Evenly Covered Neighborhoods
notes: A covering map demands that each base point own a neighborhood whose entire preimage splits into disjoint sheets, each mapped homeomorphically down. This is stronger than a local homeomorphism. The pancake stack picture makes the sheet count visible and explains why that count stays constant across a connected base.

label: The Exponential Cover
notes: The exponential map sends the real line onto the circle by winding it infinitely, placing the fiber over one point at the integer translates of any lift. Each unit interval becomes a sheet. Choosing one sheet is choosing a local section, a local inverse that picks a single branch of the angle.

label: Not Every Local Homeomorphism Covers
notes: Restricting the exponential map to the open interval gives a surjective local homeomorphism that still fails to be a covering. Near the seam point, two endpoint components cover only one side of a base arc. The defect is not local injectivity; it is the absence of complete sheets over a neighborhood.

label: Path and Homotopy Lifting
notes: Fixing a starting point in the fiber, every base path lifts uniquely, and a homotopy of base paths lifts to a homotopy upstairs holding endpoints fixed. Unique lifting forbids a connected source from silently switching sheets, so the endpoint of a lifted path is an invariant of the path-homotopy class.

label: The Lifting Criterion
notes: A map from Y lifts through a covering exactly when the fundamental-group image of Y lands inside the subgroup induced by the cover. Subgroup containment is the whole decision procedure. The condition is precisely what stops two different paths in the source from forcing two different endpoint choices for the lift.

label: Degree Divisibility
notes: For the n-fold circle cover the criterion becomes arithmetic: a degree m self-map of the circle lifts exactly when n divides m, because the cover induces the subgroup nZ and the map induces mZ. A degree seven loop over the five-fold cover ends on sheet two, since seven modulo five equals two.

label: Monodromy Action
notes: Monodromy packages all lifting from one base point into a right action of the fundamental group on a fiber. Lift a loop starting at a sheet; its endpoint sheet is the action. For the n-fold circle cover the generator cycles sheets by one step, giving a transitive action whose sheet stabilizer is nZ.

label: The Induced Injection
notes: Pushing forward along a covering map injects the fundamental group of the cover into that of the base. A loop upstairs that projects to a null-homotopic loop lifts a null-homotopy and so was already trivial. The image is the stabilizer of the chosen fiber point under the monodromy action.

label: Conjugacy and Normal Covers
notes: Changing the chosen point in a fiber conjugates the induced subgroup, so unbased covering isomorphism is naturally stated with conjugacy classes. A covering is normal when its induced subgroup is normal, equivalently when the monodromy stabilizers agree across the fiber, giving uniform deck symmetry rather than a mere conjugacy class.

label: The Universal Cover
notes: A universal cover is simply connected. Its induced subgroup is trivial, so it covers every other covering of the same base, and any two simply connected covers are isomorphic. The construction uses path classes from a base point as new points, unwrapping all fundamental-group ambiguity into distinct points upstairs.

label: Torus Lattice and RP^n
notes: For the torus the universal cover is the plane tiled by integer translates of one chart, with each fiber an integer-lattice orbit projecting by coordinate-wise modulo one. The sphere double-covers real projective space by identifying antipodes, a normal two-sheeted cover whose deck group is the order-two antipodal involution.

label: Classification of Covers
notes: Connected covers of a nice base, up to isomorphism, correspond to conjugacy classes of subgroups of the base fundamental group; based covers correspond to actual subgroups. Sheet number equals the subgroup index. The universal cover sits atop the lattice as the trivial subgroup; the base itself sits at the bottom.

label: Recap and Invariants
notes: Covering theory turns topology into subgroup arithmetic: evenly covered sheets force rigid lifting, lifting endpoints are homotopy invariants, the criterion is subgroup containment, monodromy gives transitive fiber actions with induced-subgroup stabilizers, and the universal cover anchors the classification. The circle, torus, and projective spaces supply the running computational examples.
